mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.9% compresses equity valuations through higher discount rates and reduced corporate leverage, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors shift capital to fixed income.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.9%.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate below 4.8% signals tight labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE < 4.8%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous GDP growth (GDPC1) and industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 3-month moving averages signal robust economic expansion, generating positive S&P 500 returns through synchronized demand and output growth.
failure_condition: The joint signal (GDPC1 and INDPRO above 3mo_MA) fails to produce positive returns in more than 50% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate increase exceeding 0.25% in 3 months defines an active monetary tightening cycle, reducing corporate investment and consumer spending to generate negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS increases > 0.25% in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production below 110 indicates weakening manufacturing output, reducing corporate revenue growth and investor confidence to cause negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO < 110.

mechanism_narrative: Retail sales above $380,000 million indicate strong consumer spending, supporting corporate revenue growth and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when RSAFS > 380000.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.9% triggers immediate capital reallocation to short-term fixed income, generating negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.9%.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained federal funds rate above 4.9% over 3 months compresses long-term equity valuations through persistent higher discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.9%.
